MediaTools._comment: Item 181: an absolute path to ffmpeg enables stripping metadata from audio and video. Left empty, A/V uploads keep their metadata and the feature reports itself unavailable — never a failed upload. Images are stripped regardless and need no tool. Item 186 F5b also uses this binary to sample video frames for NSFW screening; with no ffmpeg, video posts stay Pending for a moderator rather than being published unscreened.

DataProtection._comment: Where the Data Protection key ring lives. Bearer tokens from /login are protected with it, so a key ring that dies with the process silently invalidates every access AND refresh token on every restart — and the site keeps showing people as signed in while every call answers 401. Left empty, the ring goes to a 'data-protection-keys' folder beside FileStorage:RootPath, which is already required to survive a deploy and be backed up. With BOTH empty nothing is persisted and startup logs a warning naming that symptom.
DataProtection._protectKeysWith: auto (default) uses DPAPI on Windows and leaves the files unencrypted elsewhere. 'certificate' additionally needs CertificateThumbprint — and note the trap: when that certificate is replaced and removed from the store, the key ring becomes permanently unreadable, which is the mass sign-out made unrecoverable. Do not point this at a TLS certificate that auto-renews.

Cors._comment: Browser origins allowed to call this API cross-origin. Empty = same-origin deployment (reverse proxy), the preferred setup. Development overrides add the local WASM editor host. '*' is refused in code.

Smtp._comment: Outgoing mail. No secret lives here: set Smtp__Password as an environment variable (IIS: Configuration Editor → appSettings, or the app pool's environment) so it never reaches source control. With Host unset the app runs with email disabled — IEmailService.IsConfigured is false and every caller checks it.
Smtp._ports: Security=SslOnConnect pairs with port 465 (TLS from the first byte). Use StartTls with 587, or 3325 where an ISP blocks 587.

AzureAd._comment: ClientId is the REAL current registration, confirmed against the portal 2026-08-21 — an app registration id is a public identifier, not a secret. This comment previously called it a placeholder, which cost an afternoon: it is the value the website's enable-check had been given as its 'unset' sentinel, so the website hid the Microsoft button while the API stood its JWT handler up, and it was nearly added to a placeholder deny-list that would have disabled Entra permanently. If this ever does need a placeholder, write one that is NOT GUID-shaped (YOUR_CLIENT_ID) — EntraConfig.IsConfigured rejects it by shape, and nothing can tell a GUID-shaped placeholder from a real id. The file previously named the RETIRED registration e75f71ef, superseded 2026-07-18. Deployment overwrites TenantId and ClientId from C:\ishaunted-deploy\secrets.json; the client SECRET never lands in this file, it goes on the app pool as AzureAd__ClientSecret.

Serilog._comment_MinimumLevel: EF Core logs every executed SQL statement — text and parameter values — at INFORMATION, not Debug, so lowering the default does not quiet it. Measured: 654 lines of a 394 KB log, and 170 from sixteen requests. Left alone it is both the bulk of the volume and a route for row data into the log. Development turns it back up when a query needs watching. NOTE: keys inside Override are logger names, not free-form — a comment key there is read as a source and crashes startup.

Apple._comment: Sign in with Apple. ClientIds are the audiences an Apple identity token may claim — the iOS app's bundle id, plus a Services ID if the website ever offers the button. Public identifiers, not secrets. With this list EMPTY the endpoint refuses with 503 rather than validating against anything, which is how a token minted for a different app would otherwise get in.
